title: 1 Cor 11 traditions means the Gospel Paul delivered — not unwritten prayer rules
source_text: VIII. Tertius Scripturae locus, unde Pontificii pro traditionibus non scriptis argumentantur habetur: 1 Corinth. 11. ubi sic Paulus Corinthios affatur, Laudo autem vos, fratres, quod omnia mea meministis, & sicut tradidi vobis, traditiones retinetis. Dicunt enim per traditiones intelligi praecepta quaedam de modo orandi in Ecclesia, quae nusquam scripta inveniuntur. At istud non tantum dici, sed probari quoque oportuit. Nos vero dicimus per traditiones intelligi eo loco totam Evangelii doctrinam, & omnia praecepta quae a Paulo acceperant. Nam traditionis nomen, ut ante observatum fuit, generale est, & significat documenta quaevis quocunque modo tradita, seu viva voce, sive etiam scripto. Porro documentorum & institutorum illorum, quae Corinthiis primum a Paulo tradita fuerant, plurima jam tum scripta erant, alia nondum erant scripta, sed postea scripta sunt in ipsis Pauli Epistolis, & aliis Novi Testamenti libris, qui postea exarati sunt. Quaedam forte nunquam scripta fuerunt, quo in genere possunt esse ritus quidam & ceremoniae, quae ad illa tempora accommodatae erant.
pass_a_gloss: The third place of Scripture from which the Pontificians argue for unwritten traditions is found in 1 Corinthians 11, where Paul thus addresses the Corinthians, Now I praise you, brothers, that you remember me in all things, and keep the traditions as I delivered them to you. For they say that by traditions are understood certain precepts concerning the manner of praying in the Church, which are nowhere found written. But that needed not only to be said, but also to be proved. But we say that by traditions in that place is understood the whole doctrine of the Gospel, and all the precepts which they had received from Paul. For the name of tradition, as was observed before, is general, and signifies any documents handed on in whatever way, whether by living voice, or also by writing. Further, of those documents and institutions which had first been delivered by Paul to the Corinthians, many were already then written, others were not yet written, but afterward were written in Paul Epistles themselves, and in other books of the New Testament which were written later. Some perhaps were never written, in which class there can be certain rites and ceremonies which were accommodated to those times.
pass_b_english: Rome third text: 1 Cor 11 — keep the traditions as I delivered them.
They hear unwritten church-prayer rules; that needs proof, not assertion.
Tradition here means the whole Gospel and precepts Paul had given — oral or written.
Much already written, more written later in Paul and the NT; leftover rites fit their age, not a second equal rule.
